segments.text:
VVHether the child of God after repentance for some grieuous sinne, doe fall into the same againe, and come to repentance the second time. Ans. The case is dangerous, as wee may see by comparison in the bodie. If one fall into the relapse of an ague or any other strong disease, it may cost him his life: and the recouerie will bee verie hard. Christ said to the man that had bin sicke eight and thirtie yeres, after that he had healed him, Behold, thou art whole, sinne no more least a worse thing befall thee.
And the vncleane spirit returning takes to him other seauen spirits worse then himselfe. Indeede we finde no particular example of recouerie after a relapse, in the scriptures; yet no doubt a recouerie may be. Reasons are these. I. Promise is made of remission of sins in Christ without any tearme of time: without any limitation to any number or kinds of sinne: saue onely the blasphemy against the H. Ghost. Therefore there may be a repentance and saluation after a relapse. II. Christ tels Peter that he must forgiue, not til seuen times only (which peraduenture he thought to be very much) but seuentie seuen times,
and that in one daie, if one returne seuentie times and say, it repents me. Now if we must do this, which haue not so much as a drop of mercie in vs in comparison of God: hee will no doubt often forgiue, euen for one sinne, if men will returne and say, it repents me; considering that with him is plentifull redemption, and he is much in sparing.
